title: Useful Input Types
summary: Choose text, email, number, date, checkbox, radio, and other input types appropriately.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Choose a Type that Matches the Data
sketchBlocks.title: Use text, email, number, and date for the value you expect
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
The `type` attribute tells the browser what kind of value a one-line input is meant to collect. Use `text` for ordinary short text, `email` for an email address, `number` for numeric input, and `date` for a calendar date.

```html
<label for="email">Email</label>
<input id="email" name="email" type="email">
<label for="guests">Guests</label>
<input id="guests" name="guests" type="number">
```

Read this example line by line: the first label/input pair collects an email address, and the second pair collects a numeric guest count. Choosing a meaningful type gives the browser more context about the expected value.

sketchBlocks.title: Use checkbox when an option can be turned on or off independently
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
A checkbox represents an independent yes/no or on/off choice. Each checkbox should have its own label, and multiple checkboxes may all be selected at the same time.

```html
<input id="newsletter" name="newsletter" type="checkbox">
<label for="newsletter">Send me the newsletter</label>
```

Read the example line by line: the checkbox creates the independent choice, its id is `newsletter`, and the matching label explains exactly what selecting it means.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Use Radio Buttons for One Choice
sketchBlocks.title: Give related radio buttons one shared name and a group label
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Radio buttons are useful when the learner should choose exactly one option from a group. Give every radio button in the group the same `name`, give each one a unique `id` and `value`, and use `fieldset` with `legend` to describe the group.

```html
<fieldset>
  <legend>Session</legend>
  <input id="morning" name="session" type="radio" value="morning">
  <label for="morning">Morning</label>
  <input id="evening" name="session" type="radio" value="evening">
  <label for="evening">Evening</label>
</fieldset>
```

Read this example line by line: fieldset groups the choices, legend names the group, both radio inputs share `name="session"`, and each input has its own label through a unique id.
